name: Putnam-AXIOM
description: A benchmark combining 522 William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition problems with algorithmically generated functional variants created by programmatic perturbation. o1-preview scores 41.9% on original Putnam problems but drops 19.6 percentage points on functional variants — direct evidence that a substantial fraction of benchmark performance reflects memorization of competition solutions rather than genuine mathematical reasoning.
evaluation_method: accuracy (functional variant correctness; automated verification where possible)
general_score_metric: accuracy on originals vs. functional variants
typical_sota_score: o1-preview: 41.9% on originals; ~22% on functional variants (19.6 percentage point drop)
reputation: Published at ICML 2025; directly addresses contamination in university-level math evaluation; 19.6-point drop on variants provides compelling contamination evidence; Putnam is canonical undergraduate math competition
notes: ICML 2025. The William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition is the premier undergraduate mathematics competition in North America. Putnam solutions are widely published online, making contamination highly likely for models trained on internet data. Programmatic perturbation changes numerical parameters, variable names, and problem structure while preserving mathematical difficulty. The 19.6-point drop is among the largest contamination signals documented in the literature.
